data.title: ReAct
data.tagline: A task pattern where an agent decides, acts with a tool, observes the result, and decides again
data.learningOutcome: You can explain why real observations change the next action and distinguish ReAct from an agent loop.
data.description: When a login button does nothing, an agent can inspect the button first. If the click handler already exists, that observation changes the next action to inspecting the network request and its 401 response.

learning.assumes: You have seen an assistant read files, change content, and report checks.
learning.outcome: You can explain why real observations change the next action and distinguish ReAct from an agent loop.

explanation.title: Verify one concrete assumption
explanation.text: For a button that does nothing, first check whether it has a click handler.

explanation.title: Read the actual result
explanation.text: The file shows that the click handler already exists, disproving the first assumption.

explanation.title: Change the investigation
explanation.text: A 401 after the click moves the next check to authentication. This is task state, not private chain of thought.

data.boundary: ReAct is the alternation of task-level judgment, action, and observation. A tool call is one action; an agent loop controls permissions, retries, records, and stopping.

lessonPractice.title: An agent assumes a login button has no click handler, but the file shows that the handler already exists. What should happen next in a ReAct pattern?

options.label: Drop the original assumption and inspect the network request triggered by the click
options.feedback: Correct. The file result disproves the original assumption, so the next action investigates the unexplained network behavior.

options.label: Rewrite the click handler anyway because the original plan blamed the button
options.feedback: The file already shows a handler, so continuing the original edit ignores the latest evidence.

options.label: Declare the button correct and stop without checking what happens after the click
options.feedback: Clearing one location does not explain the failure; the observation should direct the next check.

data.agentPrompt: Use a ReAct pattern to diagnose this issue. State one thing to verify, perform one read or check, update the task-level conclusion from the result, and then choose the next action. If evidence disproves the original assumption, change direction instead of continuing the same edit.
